## Self-update, more platforms, current dependencies

**Security:** this release carries rustls 0.23.45, fixing [RUSTSEC-2026-0285](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0285) (TLS 1.3 handshake messages accepted across encryption-level boundaries) in 0.4.0 and earlier. Upgrade coordinators first — they terminate TLS for every member.

### `--self-update` and `--check-update`
Every binary can now update itself from GitHub releases:

```sh
nqvpn-relay --check-update   # is there a newer release? changes nothing
nqvpn-relay --self-update    # download, verify SHA-256, swap; keeps nqvpn-relay.old
```

The new binary is run once (`--version`) before it replaces anything, the swap is an atomic rename, and the running process is left alone: restart the service to pick it up. Releases before 0.5.0 do not have the flag, so this upgrade is still manual.

### Builds for more platforms
Releases are now built by GitHub Actions for Linux (static musl), macOS and FreeBSD, on amd64 and arm64. On FreeBSD the coordinator and forwarding relays are supported; the client has no TUN backend there yet. FreeBSD arm64 is built in an emulated VM and appears on the release a while after the rest.

### Console
- Generations are shown as the time they took effect everywhere, not as raw numbers: a member's view reads "OK · 09:38:25" or "behind · 09:37:10" (the generation number is still in the tooltip). Only the display changed.
- "Token secret last replaced …" and "Taken over from … at …" are now information tags on the member card, no longer flagged as problems needing attention.

### Dependencies
Everything is on its latest release: ed25519-dalek / x25519-dalek 3, rand 0.10, argon2 0.6, sha2 0.11, base64 0.23, toml 1, rusqlite 0.40, axum-server 0.8, and all compatible updates. The unmaintained `rustls-pemfile` is replaced by `rustls-pki-types`' PEM parser, and `aws-lc-rs` is no longer built (ring was already the only provider in use).

`bincode` intentionally stays on 1.3: the control plane is bincode, and a different encoding would cut every existing peer off the network. New golden tests pin credentials, keys, fingerprints, tokens, control payloads and existing argon2 password hashes byte-for-byte, so a future dependency bump cannot silently change what deployed peers and configs rely on.

**Compatibility:** no wire, token or config changes. 0.5.0 interoperates with 0.3.x and 0.4.x members, and existing `password_hash` values keep working.

| OS | amd64 | arm64 |
|---|---|---|
| Linux (static musl) | `nqvpn-0.5.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz` | `nqvpn-0.5.0-linux-arm64.tar.gz` |
| macOS | `nqvpn-0.5.0-macos-amd64.tar.gz` | `nqvpn-0.5.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz` |
| FreeBSD | `nqvpn-0.5.0-freebsd-amd64.tar.gz` | `nqvpn-0.5.0-freebsd-arm64.tar.gz` |
